summary: The root "sfk" primarily means to shed or pour forth liquids, especially blood or tears. It can also tropically refer to speaking profusely or rapidly.
lane: 1 سَفَكَ ذ , aor. سَفِكَ (S, M, O, Msb, K) and سَفُكَ , (O, Msb, TA, &c.,) inf. n. سَفْكٌ , (S, O, Msb,) He shed, poured forth, or caused to run or flow, blood, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) and tears, (S, O, Msb, TA,) and water, and any fluid or liquid, but app. most especially blood. (TA.) -b2- And [hence,] سَفَكَ الكَلَامَ , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He poured forth speech profusely, (K, TA,) with haste, or quickly. (TA.)
